title: Interview Q&A: explain code, diagnose bugs and justify design choices
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its relevant rules.
Trace the example and justify its behaviour.
Identify important assumptions and failure cases.
Apply the concept in a reviewed and tested exercise.

understand.concept: Technical interviews often ask candidates to explain code, reason about edge cases, diagnose defects and justify trade-offs. Strong answers state assumptions, trace behaviour and distinguish language guarantees from implementation details.
understand.whyItMatters: Interview preparation strengthens communication and engineering reasoning beyond memorizing definitions.
understand.analogy: Treat standards, interfaces and release steps as explicit contracts that make assumptions visible.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace the C standard, implementation documentation or project-specific requirements.

explain.narrative:
Technical interviews often ask candidates to explain code, reason about edge cases, diagnose defects and justify trade-offs. Strong answers state assumptions, trace behaviour and distinguish language guarantees from implementation details.

State assumptions and constraints, consult the applicable standard or tool documentation, and verify the result with appropriate compiler diagnostics and tests. Separate portable guarantees from implementation-specific behaviour.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: The function counts characters until the null terminator and handles a null pointer by returning zero. An interview discussion should ask whether zero is an appropriate result for NULL or whether a separate error signal would be clearer.

practise.guidedTask: Explain the function's time complexity and NULL policy.
practise.independentTask: Prepare an interview answer that explains a pointer bug, proposes a fix and describes regression tests.
hints: State assumptions before making claims about behaviour.
Compare at least one alternative and explain the trade-off.
Do not claim undefined behaviour has a predictable output.
